home.title: Golden Hour: help in the first hour after a scam
home.lead: Lost money to an online scam? The first hour matters most.
home.helpSub: Step-by-step help for the next hour
home.checkSub: Check it before you reply, pay or click

footer.disclaimer: Not a government service. Not legal advice. Nothing you type here leaves your phone.

help.title: Lost money? Do these now
help.lead: Do them in this order. Even if hours or days have passed, still do every step.

steps.title: Call 1930
steps.body: Say you lost money in online fraud. Keep your bank SMS open: they will ask for the amount, the time and the transaction ID (UTR). Write down the complaint number they give you.

steps.title: Block your card and UPI
steps.body: Call your bank on the number printed on your card or shown in the bank's own app. Never use a number that came in a message or a search ad.

steps.title: Finish the complaint online within 24 hours
steps.body: On cybercrime.gov.in, choose financial fraud and enter your 1930 complaint number. Add screenshots of the transaction and the chat.

steps.title: Tell your bank in writing
steps.body: Use the bank app's fraud option or email the bank, and keep the complaint number. For frauds from 1 January 2027, tell your bank and 1930 within 5 days: small losses may then be compensated.

steps.title: Keep every proof
steps.body: Do not delete messages, chats, call logs or the scammer's UPI ID. Take screenshots now.

help.noLossBody: Report the call or message on Chakshu (sancharsaathi.gov.in) so the number can be blocked.

check.title: Check a message
check.label: Paste the message here
check.fallback: The automatic check needs JavaScript. Until then, stop if a message:
signs: asks for an OTP, PIN or password
asks you to pay first to get money, a job or a prize
threatens arrest, a blocked account or a cut connection, and rushes you
has a link or an app you were not expecting
check.copied: Copied. Paste it to someone you trust.
check.empty: Paste or share a message first.
check.shareIntro: Is this message real? Please take a look before I reply:
check.copyFail: The message is selected. Copy it and send it to someone you trust.
check.disclaimer: This check runs on your phone and can be wrong. Not legal advice. Rules are drafts until checked against official advisories.

likely.title: Likely scam
likely.body: Do not pay, click, reply or share any code.

careful.title: Be careful
careful.body: Some scam signs. Before you act, check with your bank or family on a number you already know.

none.title: No common scam signs found
none.body: This does not mean it is safe. If it asks for money, an OTP or an app install, stop.

kyc.name: KYC update or account block
kyc.rule: Banks never ask you to update KYC through a link in a message.

arrest.name: Police, CBI or customs (digital arrest)
arrest.rule: No agency arrests anyone or collects money over a video call.

parcel.name: Parcel or customs fee
parcel.rule: Pay delivery charges only inside the courier's own app.

bill.name: Electricity or bill disconnection
bill.rule: Pay bills only through the provider's own app or website.

job.name: Job or task offer
job.rule: A real employer never asks you to pay to get or keep a job.

invest.name: Investment or trading group
invest.rule: Guaranteed high returns from a WhatsApp group are a scam.

loan.name: Loan app
loan.rule: Lenders must be RBI-registered; never install a lending app from a link.

prize.name: Prize, lottery or refund
prize.rule: You cannot win something you never entered.

otp.name: OTP or screen-sharing request
otp.rule: Never share an OTP or install a screen-sharing app for anyone.

family.name: Family emergency
family.rule: Call the family member on their known number before paying.

threat.name: Threat or sextortion
threat.rule: Do not pay; report at cybercrime.gov.in.

unknown.name: Suspicious message
unknown.rule: Do not open links or install apps from a message you did not expect.

signNames.apk: A link to install an app file (.apk)
signNames.screenShare: Asks you to install a screen-sharing app
signNames.otpAsk: Asks for an OTP, PIN or password
signNames.collect: Asks you to enter your UPI PIN or approve a request to receive money
signNames.lookalike: A link pretending to be a bank, company or government site
signNames.shortLink: A shortened link that hides where it goes
signNames.unknownLink: A link to a website that is not a known official site
signNames.money: Asks you to pay or send money

terms.title: Terms
body: Golden Hour is an independent open-source project. It is not run by or connected to the Government of India, I4C, RBI or any bank.
It gives general information from official public sources. It is not legal or financial advice, and it cannot recover money.
Always follow the instructions of the 1930 operator, the police and your bank.
The checker can be wrong. A message it does not flag can still be a scam.
Use it at your own risk. The software is provided as is, under the MIT licence.

privacy.title: Privacy
body: Golden Hour has no server that receives what you type, paste or share. Everything is processed on your phone.
The app keeps no history. A message you share to it is kept on your phone only until the next page opens, then deleted.
There are no accounts, cookies, ads or analytics.
Shares are handled on your phone by the installed app. If the app's stored files were cleared, open the app once before sharing; otherwise a share can reach our web host, which rejects it.
Links to cybercrime.gov.in, sancharsaathi.gov.in and your phone dialer open outside the app.
